@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claim that orca.nix runs the Orca GUI unsandboxed: the
+# AppImage's tree patched with autoPatchelf and wrapped with makeWrapper, not
+# appimageTools' bwrap FHS env.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Inside the FHS env, everything Orca spawns -- its
+# terminals and the agents in them -- saw the env's /usr, not the host's:
+# /etc/hostname was missing, `date` printed UTC (/etc/localtime points into
+# /usr/share/zoneinfo), every font fell to Montserrat Thin. And bwrap stood
+# between every caller and Electron, forwarding no signals. None of that shows
+# from the host, only from a process the app spawns, so these cases probe from
+# one.
+#
+# The probes run on the host. When this script itself runs inside a sandbox
+# (an Orca terminal on the old build has no /etc/hostname), each probe goes
+# through `systemd-run --user`, whose units the user manager starts outside it.
+#
+# Two trees are deliberately left unpatched and must stay byte-identical:
+# resources/node-runtime, whose node is copied into orcad slots and checked
+# against a sha256 pin in app.asar (a patched node fails the check, and Orca
+# falls back to downloading stock node), and resources/orcad-template, whose
+# per-target builds (arm64, musl) are shipped to remote hosts.
+#
+# The GUI case (6) opens a real, visible window on the desktop, so it runs
+# only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 -- ask before setting it on someone's session.
+# It starts a second instance with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway
+# HOME, so it never touches the running Orca's profile, its
+# ~/.orca/agent-hooks or ~/.claude/settings.json.
+#
+#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
+#   ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh   ... and launch it once
+#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh <orca-path>   test a given build, e.g. the live one:
+#                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+
+if [ -e /etc/hostname ]; then
+  host() { "$@"; }
+else
+  sr=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" 'nixpkgs#systemd^out') \
+    || { echo "inside a sandbox and could not build systemd-run" >&2; exit 1; }
+  # Through /bin/sh, so the command is looked up on the host's PATH, not here.
+  host() { "$sr/bin/systemd-run" --user --pipe --wait --quiet /bin/sh -c 'exec "$@"' sh "$@"; }
+fi
+HOSTNAME_=$(host cat /etc/hostname) || { echo "cannot reach the host" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+ORCA="${1:-}"
+if [ -z "$ORCA" ]; then
+  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$HOSTNAME_.config.home.packages" \

+node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode

+    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
+    "$1" 2>&1

+  want=$(host /bin/sh -c "$c"); got=$(node_run "$c")

+  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"

+# stripped, no shebang rewritten. The derivation's src is the extracted
+# AppImage, so it is on this machine whenever the build is.

+  | grep -oE '"src": *"/nix/store/[^"]*-extracted"' | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^"]*')

+  || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"

+# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.

+  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
+elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then

+  since=$(date +%s)

+    --setenv=HOME="$T/home" "$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"

+    sleep 1
+    pids=$(host systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
+    [ -n "$pids" ] && [ "$pids" != 0 ] \
+      && host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids," && break
+  done

+    || fail "chromium sandbox" "renderers: '${ns:-none}'"

+    res=$(host systemctl --user show -p Result --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
+    res=${res:-success}
+  else
+    res="stop failed"
+  fi
+  host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
+  [ "$res" = success ] && pass "stops cleanly on SIGTERM" \
+    || fail "SIGTERM" "unit result '$res'"

+  [ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
+fi
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claim that orca.nix runs the Orca GUI unsandboxed: the
+# AppImage's tree patched with autoPatchelf and wrapped with makeWrapper, not
+# appimageTools' bwrap FHS env.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Inside the FHS env, everything Orca spawns -- its
+# terminals and the agents in them -- saw the env's /usr, not the host's:
+# /etc/hostname was missing, `date` printed UTC (/etc/localtime points into
+# /usr/share/zoneinfo), every font fell to Montserrat Thin. And bwrap stood
+# between every caller and Electron, forwarding no signals. None of that shows
+# from the host, only from a process the app spawns, so these cases probe from
+# one.
+#
+# The probes run on the host. When this script itself runs inside a sandbox
+# (an Orca terminal on the old build has no /etc/hostname), each probe goes
+# through `systemd-run --user`, whose units the user manager starts outside it.
+#
+# Two trees are deliberately left unpatched and must stay byte-identical:
+# resources/node-runtime, whose node is copied into orcad slots and checked
+# against a sha256 pin in app.asar (a patched node fails the check, and Orca
+# falls back to downloading stock node), and resources/orcad-template, whose
+# per-target builds (arm64, musl) are shipped to remote hosts.
+#
+# The GUI case (6) opens a real, visible window on the desktop, so it runs
+# only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 -- ask before setting it on someone's session.
+# It starts a second instance with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway
+# HOME, so it never touches the running Orca's profile, its
+# ~/.orca/agent-hooks or ~/.claude/settings.json.
+#
+#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
+#   ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh   ... and launch it once
+#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh <orca-path>   test a given build, e.g. the live one:
+#                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+
+if [ -e /etc/hostname ]; then
+  host() { "$@"; }
+else
+  sr=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" 'nixpkgs#systemd^out') \
+    || { echo "inside a sandbox and could not build systemd-run" >&2; exit 1; }
+  # Through /bin/sh, so the command is looked up on the host's PATH, not here.
+  host() { "$sr/bin/systemd-run" --user --pipe --wait --quiet /bin/sh -c 'exec "$@"' sh "$@"; }
+fi
+HOSTNAME_=$(host cat /etc/hostname) || { echo "cannot reach the host" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+ORCA="${1:-}"
+if [ -z "$ORCA" ]; then
+  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$HOSTNAME_.config.home.packages" \
+    --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: builtins.match "orca-[0-9.]+" (p.name or "") != null) ps)).drvPath') \
+    || { echo "orca is not in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+  ORCA=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+fi
+ORCA=$(readlink -f "$ORCA")
+
+# The desktop file's Exec names the GUI bin, whatever it is called this week.
+exe=$(sed -n 's/^Exec=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$ORCA"/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop | head -1)
+GUI="$ORCA/bin/$exe"
+[ -n "$exe" ] && [ -x "$GUI" ] || { echo "no GUI bin from $ORCA's desktop Exec ('$exe')" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $GUI"
+
+T=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.cache/orca-gui-test.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
+if nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | grep -q -- '-bubblewrap-'; then
+  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"
+else
+  pass "no bubblewrap in the closure"
+fi
+
+# The unwrapped tree: where resources/ lives.
+APP=$(nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/lib/orca/resources/app.asar" ] && echo "$p/lib/orca"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$APP" ] || { fail "layout" "no lib/orca/resources/app.asar in the closure"; APP=/nonexistent; }
+
+# 2. Node mode: the wrapper must not inject --ozone-platform, which node
+# rejects ("bad option", exit 9). orca's CLI probes the GUI this way.
+got=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -p 1 2>&1)
+[ "$got" = 1 ] && pass "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 runs node" \
+  || fail "node mode" "printed '$got', want 1"
+
+# 3. What a spawned process sees is the host: hostname, zone, fonts.
+node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode
+  host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \
+    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
+    "$1" 2>&1
+}
+for c in 'cat /etc/hostname' 'date +%Z' 'readlink /etc/localtime'; do
+  want=$(host /bin/sh -c "$c"); got=$(node_run "$c")
+  [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "child sees host's '$c' ($want)" \
+    || fail "$c" "child got '$got', host has '$want'"
+done
+# Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono", one
+# family with no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another
+# mono font; the host has no DejaVu, so orca.nix's fontsConf must apply.
+got=$(node_run "fc-list -f '%{family[0]}\n' 'DejaVu Sans Mono' | sort -u | head -1")
+[ "$got" = "DejaVu Sans Mono" ] && pass "'DejaVu Sans Mono' exists for the app (terminal default)" \
+  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"
+for c in 'sans\-serif:Noto Sans' 'monospace:Noto Sans Mono'; do
+  pat=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
+  got=$(node_run "fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' '$pat'")
+  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$pat -> $want for the app" \
+    || fail "$pat" "resolves to '${got:-nothing}', want '$want'"
+done
+
+# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty, loaded by this Electron, opens a pty.
+got=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
+  const p = require(process.argv[1]).spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "echo pty-ok"], {});
+  let o = ""; p.onData(d => o += d); p.onExit(e => console.log(o.trim(), e.exitCode));' \
+  "$APP/resources/node_modules/node-pty" 2>&1)
+[ "$got" = "pty-ok 0" ] && pass "node-pty opens a pty" || fail "node-pty" "got '$got'"
+
+# 4. Every native ELF of this arch resolves all its libraries on the host.
+mapfile -t elfs < <(find "$APP" -type f \( -name '*.so*' -o -name '*.node' -o -perm -u+x \) \
+  -not -path '*/orcad-template/*' -print0 \
+  | host xargs -0 file | grep -E 'ELF 64-bit LSB .*(executable|shared object), x86-64' | cut -d: -f1)
+if [ "${#elfs[@]}" -lt 10 ]; then
+  fail "ELFs" "only ${#elfs[@]} found under $APP"
+else
+  missing=$(host /bin/sh -c 'for f; do ldd "$f" 2>&1 | grep "not found" | sed "s|^|$f: |"; done' sh "${elfs[@]}")
+  [ -z "$missing" ] && pass "all ${#elfs[@]} ELFs resolve their libraries" \
+    || fail "ldd" "$(printf '\n%s' "$missing")"
+fi
+
+# 5. The pinned trees are the AppImage's, byte for byte -- not patched, not
+# stripped, no shebang rewritten. The derivation's src is the extracted
+# AppImage, so it is on this machine whenever the build is.
+src=$(nix derivation show "$(nix-store -qd "$APP/../..")" 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -oE '"src": *"/nix/store/[^"]*-extracted"' | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^"]*')
+if [ -z "$src" ]; then
+  fail "pinned trees" "cannot find the derivation's src for $APP"
+else
+  for d in resources/node-runtime resources/orcad-template; do
+    if out=$(diff -r "$src/$d" "$APP/$d" 2>&1); then
+      pass "$d is the AppImage's, unchanged"
+    else
+      fail "$d" "differs from $src: $(echo "$out" | head -3)"
+    fi
+  done
+fi
+node="$APP/resources/node-runtime/bin/node"
+# The slot's runtime reference: what orcad checks the copied node against.
+pin=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$APP/resources/orcad-template/targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node" 2>/dev/null)
+got=$(sha256sum "$node" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)
+[ -n "$pin" ] && [ "$got" = "$pin" ] && pass "bundled node matches orcad's runtime pin" \
+  || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"
+
+# 6. A real second instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and stops on
+# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.
+if [ "${ORCA_TEST_GUI:-}" != 1 ]; then
+  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
+elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then
+  echo "skip GUI launch: no Wayland session"
+else
+  unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
+  mkdir -p "$T/home"
+  since=$(date +%s)
+  "${sr:+$sr/bin/}systemd-run" --user --quiet --unit="$unit" --property=KillSignal=SIGTERM \
+    --setenv=HOME="$T/home" "$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"
+  pids=""
+  for _ in $(seq 40); do
+    sleep 1
+    pids=$(host systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
+    [ -n "$pids" ] && [ "$pids" != 0 ] \
+      && host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids," && break
+  done
+  if host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids,"; then
+    pass "a window maps (pid $pids)"
+  else
+    fail "window" "no Hyprland client for pid '$pids' after 40s"
+    host journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager -n 20
+  fi
+  # Renderers in their own user namespace = Chromium's namespace sandbox,
+  # with chrome-sandbox left unprivileged.
+  ns=$(host /bin/sh -c '
+    main=$(readlink /proc/'"$pids"'/ns/user)
+    for p in $(systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value '"$unit"' | xargs -I{} cat /sys/fs/cgroup{}/cgroup.procs); do
+      tr "\0" " " < /proc/$p/cmdline | grep -q -- "--type=renderer" || continue
+      [ "$(readlink /proc/$p/ns/user)" != "$main" ] && echo sandboxed || echo unsandboxed
+    done' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
+  [ "$ns" = "sandboxed " ] && pass "renderers run in their own user namespace" \
+    || fail "chromium sandbox" "renderers: '${ns:-none}'"
+  # A transient unit that stopped cleanly is unloaded (show prints nothing);
+  # one whose main process exited non-zero stays loaded as failed, with why.
+  if host systemctl --user stop "$unit"; then
+    res=$(host systemctl --user show -p Result --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
+    res=${res:-success}
+  else
+    res="stop failed"
+  fi
+  host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
+  [ "$res" = success ] && pass "stops cleanly on SIGTERM" \
+    || fail "SIGTERM" "unit result '$res'"
+  cores=$(host coredumpctl list --no-legend --since="@$since" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "$ORCA|orca-ide" || true)
+  [ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
+fi
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

1	{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:
     2	
     3	let
     4	  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
     5	  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;
     6	
     7	  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
     8	  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
     9	  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
    10	  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
    11	  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
    12	  # is the AppImage's, checked against
    13	  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
    14	  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
    15	  pname = "orca";
    16	  version = "1.4.238";
    17	  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    18	    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    19	    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
    20	  };
    21	
    22	  # The AppImage's own tree, unsandboxed: its ELFs patched to store paths with
    23	  # autoPatchelf and the binary wrapped with makeWrapper, the way nixpkgs
    24	  # packages slack or vscode. A patched binary runs on Arch as well as NixOS.
    25	  # This replaced appimageTools.wrapType2, whose bwrap FHS env everything Orca
    26	  # spawns (its terminals, the agents in them) inherited: no /etc/hostname,
    27	  # `date` in UTC (/etc/localtime points into a /usr the env replaced), fonts
    28	  # dangling, and bwrap between every caller and Electron, forwarding no
    29	  # signals. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh.
    30	  #
    31	  # Two trees stay byte-identical. resources/node-runtime's node is copied
    32	  # into orcad slots and checked against a sha256 pin (the template's
    33	  # targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node); patched -- or stripped -- it
    34	  # fails the check and Orca downloads stock node instead. resources/
    35	  # orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca ships to
    36	  # remote hosts. Both run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader, which
    37	  # Arch is. The AppImage's own usr/lib (libnotify, libappindicator, ...) is
    38	  # left out for nixpkgs' copies, below.
    39	  #
    40	  # chrome-sandbox ships without the setuid bit (the store cannot hold one);
    41	  # with unprivileged user namespaces, which Arch has, Chromium uses its
    42	  # namespace sandbox and never needs it.
    43	  orca = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation {
    44	    inherit pname version;
    45	    src = appimageContents;
    46	    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.autoPatchelfHook pkgs.makeWrapper ];
    47	    buildInputs = with pkgs; [
    48	      alsa-lib at-spi2-atk cairo cups dbus expat glib gtk3 libdrm libgbm
    49	      libxkbcommon nspr nss pango stdenv.cc.cc.lib systemd
    50	      libx11 libxcomposite libxdamage libxext libxfixes libxrandr libxcb
    51	    ];
    52	    # dlopened, so autoPatchelf cannot see them: GL and udev for the GPU
    53	    # process, libsecret for Electron's safeStorage, notify and appindicator
    54	    # for notifications and the tray.
    55	    runtimeDependencies = with pkgs; [
    56	      libGL systemd libsecret libnotify libappindicator-gtk3
    57	    ];
    58	    dontConfigure = true;
    59	    dontBuild = true;
    60	    # Both run by hand, or not at all, around the pinned trees: strip would
    61	    # rewrite the pinned node as surely as patchelf.
    62	    dontAutoPatchelf = true;
    63	    dontStrip = true;
    64	    installPhase = ''
    65	      runHook preInstall
    66	      mkdir -p $out/lib/orca $out/share/applications
    67	      cp -r --no-preserve=ownership . $out/lib/orca
    68	      chmod -R u+w $out/lib/orca
    69	      rm -r $out/lib/orca/{AppRun,.DirIcon,usr,orca-ide.desktop,orca-ide.png}
    70	      install -Dm444 orca-ide.desktop $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
    71	      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
    72	        install -Dm444 usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
    73	          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
    74	      done
    75	      # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    76	      # names the app orca-ide, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    77	      # meta.mainProgram use.
    78	      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
    79	        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    80	      runHook postInstall
    81	    '';
    82	    postFixup = ''
    83	      targets=()
    84	      for p in $out/lib/orca/* $out/lib/orca/resources/*; do
    85	        case $p in
    86	          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template) ;;
    87	          *) targets+=("$p") ;;
    88	        esac
    89	      done
    90	      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
    91	
    92	      # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    93	      # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and
    94	      # on a Hyprland-only session there is no X server -- a bare launch exits
    95	      # 1 with "needs a usable display server". A flag, not an env var, so a
    96	      # desktop-file launch gets it too. Not in node mode: node rejects it
    97	      # ("bad option", exit 9), and Orca's CLI runs this binary that way.
    98	      #
    99	      # FONTCONFIG_FILE: Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly
   100	      # "DejaVu Sans Mono", which the host's fontconfig lacks; see fontsConf.
   101	      #
   102	      # A plain exec: signals and exit codes reach Electron directly.
   103	      makeWrapper $out/lib/orca/orca-ide $out/bin/orca-ide \
   104	        --set FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf} \
   105	        --run '[ -n "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE-}" ] || set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"'
   106	    '';
   107	    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
   108	  };
   109	  # The app's fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here gets a
   110	  # nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE instead of the distro's. Hermetic: nixpkgs'
   111	  # own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set), whose 50-user.conf
   112	  # pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font dirs, i.e. the
   113	  # nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu, which the host
   114	  # does not have:
   115	  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
   116	  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
   117	  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
   118	  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
   119	  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
   120	    <?xml version="1.0"?>
   121	    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
   122	    <fontconfig>
   123	      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
   124	      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
   125	      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
   126	    </fontconfig>
   127	  '';
   128	  # Extracted once, shared by orca and macKeybindings; let bindings
   129	  # are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
   130	  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
   131	
   132	  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
   133	  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
   134	  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
   135	  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
   136	  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own
   137	  # (Ctrl+1..9 tab select, Alt+Z word wrap, Ctrl+PageUp/Down), not a Linux
   138	  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,
   139	  # and the few orcaPinned below puts back on purpose.
   140	  #

     4	  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;

     7	  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
     8	  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
     9	  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
    10	  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
    11	  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
    12	  # is the AppImage's, checked against
    13	  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
    14	  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
    15	  pname = "orca";
    16	  version = "1.4.238";
    17	  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    18	    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    19	    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
    20	  };
    21	
    22	  # The AppImage's own tree, unsandboxed: its ELFs patched to store paths with
    23	  # autoPatchelf and the binary wrapped with makeWrapper, the way nixpkgs
    24	  # packages slack or vscode. A patched binary runs on Arch as well as NixOS.
    25	  # This replaced appimageTools.wrapType2, whose bwrap FHS env everything Orca
    26	  # spawns (its terminals, the agents in them) inherited: no /etc/hostname,
    27	  # `date` in UTC (/etc/localtime points into a /usr the env replaced), fonts
    28	  # dangling, and bwrap between every caller and Electron, forwarding no
    29	  # signals. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh.
    30	  #
    31	  # Two trees stay byte-identical. resources/node-runtime's node is copied
    32	  # into orcad slots and checked against a sha256 pin (the template's
    33	  # targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node); patched -- or stripped -- it
    34	  # fails the check and Orca downloads stock node instead. resources/
    35	  # orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca ships to
    36	  # remote hosts. Both run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader, which
    37	  # Arch is. The AppImage's own usr/lib (libnotify, libappindicator, ...) is
    38	  # left out for nixpkgs' copies, below.
    39	  #
    40	  # chrome-sandbox ships without the setuid bit (the store cannot hold one);
    41	  # with unprivileged user namespaces, which Arch has, Chromium uses its
    42	  # namespace sandbox and never needs it.
    43	  orca = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation {
    44	    inherit pname version;
    45	    src = appimageContents;
    46	    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.autoPatchelfHook pkgs.makeWrapper ];
    47	    buildInputs = with pkgs; [
    48	      alsa-lib at-spi2-atk cairo cups dbus expat glib gtk3 libdrm libgbm
    49	      libxkbcommon nspr nss pango stdenv.cc.cc.lib systemd
    50	      libx11 libxcomposite libxdamage libxext libxfixes libxrandr libxcb
    51	    ];
    52	    # dlopened, so autoPatchelf cannot see them: GL and udev for the GPU
    53	    # process, libsecret for Electron's safeStorage, notify and appindicator
    54	    # for notifications and the tray.
    55	    runtimeDependencies = with pkgs; [
    56	      libGL systemd libsecret libnotify libappindicator-gtk3
    57	    ];
    58	    dontConfigure = true;
    59	    dontBuild = true;
    60	    # Both run by hand, or not at all, around the pinned trees: strip would
    61	    # rewrite the pinned node as surely as patchelf.
    62	    dontAutoPatchelf = true;
    63	    dontStrip = true;
    64	    installPhase = ''
    65	      runHook preInstall
    66	      mkdir -p $out/lib/orca $out/share/applications
    67	      cp -r --no-preserve=ownership . $out/lib/orca
    68	      chmod -R u+w $out/lib/orca
    69	      rm -r $out/lib/orca/{AppRun,.DirIcon,usr,orca-ide.desktop,orca-ide.png}
    70	      install -Dm444 orca-ide.desktop $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
    71	      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
    72	        install -Dm444 usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
    73	          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
    74	      done
    75	      # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    76	      # names the app orca-ide, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    77	      # meta.mainProgram use.
    78	      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
    79	        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    80	      runHook postInstall
    81	    '';
    82	    postFixup = ''
    83	      targets=()
    84	      for p in $out/lib/orca/* $out/lib/orca/resources/*; do
    85	        case $p in
    86	          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template) ;;
    87	          *) targets+=("$p") ;;
    88	        esac
    89	      done
    90	      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
    91	
    92	      # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    93	      # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and
    94	      # on a Hyprland-only session there is no X server -- a bare launch exits
    95	      # 1 with "needs a usable display server". A flag, not an env var, so a
    96	      # desktop-file launch gets it too. Not in node mode: node rejects it
    97	      # ("bad option", exit 9), and Orca's CLI runs this binary that way.
    98	      #
    99	      # FONTCONFIG_FILE: Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly
   100	      # "DejaVu Sans Mono", which the host's fontconfig lacks; see fontsConf.
   101	      #
   102	      # A plain exec: signals and exit codes reach Electron directly.
   103	      makeWrapper $out/lib/orca/orca-ide $out/bin/orca-ide \
   104	        --set FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf} \
   105	        --run '[ -n "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE-}" ] || set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"'
   106	    '';
   107	    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
   108	  };
   109	  # The app's fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here gets a
   110	  # nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE instead of the distro's. Hermetic: nixpkgs'
   111	  # own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set), whose 50-user.conf
   112	  # pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font dirs, i.e. the
   113	  # nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu, which the host
   114	  # does not have:
   115	  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
   116	  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
   117	  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
   118	  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
   119	  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
   120	    <?xml version="1.0"?>
   121	    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
   122	    <fontconfig>
   123	      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
   124	      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
   125	      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
   126	    </fontconfig>
   127	  '';

   129	  # are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
   130	  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
   131	
   132	  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
   133	  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
   134	  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
   135	  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
   136	  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own

   138	  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,

1	{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:
     2	
     3	let
     4	  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
     5	  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;
     6	
     7	  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
     8	  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
     9	  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
    10	  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
    11	  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
    12	  # is the AppImage's, checked against
    13	  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
    14	  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
    15	  pname = "orca";
    16	  version = "1.4.238";
    17	  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    18	    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    19	    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
    20	  };
    21	
    22	  # The AppImage's own tree, unsandboxed: its ELFs patched to store paths with
    23	  # autoPatchelf and the binary wrapped with makeWrapper, the way nixpkgs
    24	  # packages slack or vscode. A patched binary runs on Arch as well as NixOS.
    25	  # This replaced appimageTools.wrapType2, whose bwrap FHS env everything Orca
    26	  # spawns (its terminals, the agents in them) inherited: no /etc/hostname,
    27	  # `date` in UTC (/etc/localtime points into a /usr the env replaced), fonts
    28	  # dangling, and bwrap between every caller and Electron, forwarding no
    29	  # signals. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh.
    30	  #
    31	  # Two trees stay byte-identical. resources/node-runtime's node is copied
    32	  # into orcad slots and checked against a sha256 pin (the template's
    33	  # targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node); patched -- or stripped -- it
    34	  # fails the check and Orca downloads stock node instead. resources/
    35	  # orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca ships to
    36	  # remote hosts. Both run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader, which
    37	  # Arch is. The AppImage's own usr/lib (libnotify, libappindicator, ...) is
    38	  # left out for nixpkgs' copies, below.
    39	  #
    40	  # chrome-sandbox ships without the setuid bit (the store cannot hold one);
    41	  # with unprivileged user namespaces, which Arch has, Chromium uses its
    42	  # namespace sandbox and never needs it.
    43	  orca = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation {
    44	    inherit pname version;
    45	    src = appimageContents;
    46	    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.autoPatchelfHook pkgs.makeWrapper ];
    47	    buildInputs = with pkgs; [
    48	      alsa-lib at-spi2-atk cairo cups dbus expat glib gtk3 libdrm libgbm
    49	      libxkbcommon nspr nss pango stdenv.cc.cc.lib systemd
    50	      libx11 libxcomposite libxdamage libxext libxfixes libxrandr libxcb
    51	    ];
    52	    # dlopened, so autoPatchelf cannot see them: GL and udev for the GPU
    53	    # process, libsecret for Electron's safeStorage, notify and appindicator
    54	    # for notifications and the tray.
    55	    runtimeDependencies = with pkgs; [
    56	      libGL systemd libsecret libnotify libappindicator-gtk3
    57	    ];
    58	    dontConfigure = true;
    59	    dontBuild = true;
    60	    # Both run by hand, or not at all, around the pinned trees: strip would
    61	    # rewrite the pinned node as surely as patchelf.
    62	    dontAutoPatchelf = true;
    63	    dontStrip = true;
    64	    installPhase = ''
    65	      runHook preInstall
    66	      mkdir -p $out/lib/orca $out/share/applications
    67	      cp -r --no-preserve=ownership . $out/lib/orca
    68	      chmod -R u+w $out/lib/orca
    69	      rm -r $out/lib/orca/{AppRun,.DirIcon,usr,orca-ide.desktop,orca-ide.png}
    70	      install -Dm444 orca-ide.desktop $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
    71	      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
    72	        install -Dm444 usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
    73	          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
    74	      done
    75	      # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    76	      # names the app orca-ide, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    77	      # meta.mainProgram use.
    78	      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
    79	        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    80	      runHook postInstall
    81	    '';
    82	    postFixup = ''
    83	      targets=()
    84	      for p in $out/lib/orca/* $out/lib/orca/resources/*; do
    85	        case $p in
    86	          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template) ;;
    87	          *) targets+=("$p") ;;
    88	        esac
    89	      done
    90	      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
    91	
    92	      # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    93	      # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and
    94	      # on a Hyprland-only session there is no X server -- a bare launch exits
    95	      # 1 with "needs a usable display server". A flag, not an env var, so a
    96	      # desktop-file launch gets it too. Not in node mode: node rejects it
    97	      # ("bad option", exit 9), and Orca's CLI runs this binary that way.
    98	      #
    99	      # FONTCONFIG_FILE: Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly
   100	      # "DejaVu Sans Mono", which the host's fontconfig lacks; see fontsConf.
   101	      #
   102	      # A plain exec: signals and exit codes reach Electron directly.
   103	      makeWrapper $out/lib/orca/orca-ide $out/bin/orca-ide \
   104	        --set FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf} \
   105	        --run '[ -n "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE-}" ] || set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"'
   106	    '';
   107	    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
   108	  };
   109	  # The app's fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here gets a
   110	  # nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE instead of the distro's. Hermetic: nixpkgs'
   111	  # own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set), whose 50-user.conf
   112	  # pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font dirs, i.e. the
   113	  # nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu, which the host
   114	  # does not have:
   115	  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
   116	  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
   117	  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
   118	  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
   119	  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
   120	    <?xml version="1.0"?>
   121	    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
   122	    <fontconfig>
   123	      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
   124	      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
   125	      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
   126	    </fontconfig>
   127	  '';
   128	  # Extracted once, shared by orca and macKeybindings; let bindings
   129	  # are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
   130	  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
   131	
   132	  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
   133	  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
   134	  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
   135	  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
   136	  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own
   137	  # (Ctrl+1..9 tab select, Alt+Z word wrap, Ctrl+PageUp/Down), not a Linux
   138	  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,
   139	  # and the few orcaPinned below puts back on purpose.
   140	  #

#!/nix/store/nnm9gdr70ihc6zc9298mzz8jpcgaciql-bash-5.3p20/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"
---
"postFixup":"targets=()\nfor p in $out/lib/orca/* $out/lib/orca/resources/*; do\n  case $p in\n    */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template) ;;\n    *) targets+=(\"$p\") ;;\n  esac\ndone\nautoPatchelf -- \"${targets[@]}\"\n\n# --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither\n# --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise
"src":"/nix/store/k0m448kgqa8i0mhksvz488q9663d0g99-orca-1.4.238-extracted"

Host-membership lists and package-build smoke tests used to be in here and are
not any more: a drifted host gate shows up the first time you run the tool, and
what a build produced belongs to that derivation's own `installCheckPhase`,
where it gates the build instead of being checked after the fact.

```bash
./tests/hyprlock-faillock.sh     # builds the script, then drives 33 cases
./tests/system-packages.sh       # sources system/pacman.sh, drives 26 cases
./tests/net-tools.sh             # each net command against the package shipping it, per host
./tests/cjk-fonts.sh             # CJK font in every host, and fontconfig sees ja/ko/zh
./tests/sandbox-fonts.sh         # orca's real bwrap launcher resolves sans/Arial/monospace like the host
./tests/ligature-nerd-font.sh    # JetBrainsMono Nerd Font installed, with powerline glyphs and ligatures (calt)
./tests/brotli-cve-2026-111497.sh # every node in the profile loads a libbrotlidec with the fix
./tests/system-secrets.sh        # sources system/secrets.sh, drives 20 cases
./tests/thermald-setup.sh        # drives 8 cases against system/thermald-setup
./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh   # drives 13 cases against the live zsh config
./tests/zsh-compinit-once.sh     # drives 4 cases against the live zsh config
./tests/hms-ci-poll.sh           # drives 29 cases against the built hms
./tests/hmeval.sh                # drives 27 cases against the built hmeval
./tests/hyprland-zen-popup.sh    # drives 7 cases against the live generated hyprland.lua
./tests/polkit-agent.sh          # evaluates 5 hosts + a synthetic one, 17 cases
./tests/insecure-packages.sh     # 2 cases per host, plus mari's darwin system
./tests/gnome-keyring-seal.sh    # builds the script, drives 14 cases with stub tpm2
./tests/elephant-reindex.sh      # renders each walker host's unit, plus sd-switch's job type
f888db7d orca: run the GUI unsandboxed, autoPatchelf instead of bwrap
39c256fd orca: say what Alt+Up/Down takes, and that pins are the exception
40345fda orca: previous/next worktree on Alt+Up/Down
7f830873 orca: Ctrl+PageUp/Down are the terminal's too
812a220e orca: leave Ctrl and Meta to the terminal; find on Ctrl+S
8904bc2d orca: build-time merge check asserts the generated table, not a hard-coded chord
c92d99f7 orca: unmappable Hyprland binds no longer fail the build
2a2d3562 orca: keybinding merge keeps a UI value that equals a generated one as the UI's

mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sauyon-orca-workspaces-dotfiles-orca-gui-unsandbox/0f356773-2907-467c-ac73-3e2219018d85/scratchpad && cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sauyon-orca-workspaces-dotfiles-orca-gui-unsandbox/0f356773-2907-467c-ac73-3e2219018d85/scratchpad/review-r1-security.md <<'EOF'
# Review r1: security and quality, `git diff 39c256fd..HEAD` (f888db7d)

The working tree is clean (`git status`: nothing to commit). I inspected the built output: za7q6... is the nixGL symlinkJoin, and the inner build is /nix/store/hpcdlg163wysqyp2qy55xpqql3776sdk-orca-1.4.238. I did not launch the GUI.

## Critical
None.

## Important

**I1. README.md:112 still lists the deleted test.**
`./tests/sandbox-fonts.sh  # orca's real bwrap launcher resolves sans/Arial/monospace like the host`. Anyone who copies the README's test list gets "No such file". Replace it with `./tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh` and a one-line summary in the same style. No other stale bwrap, extraInstallCommands or sandbox-fonts references are left in tracked files (the .drovr/ hits are review artifacts).

**I2. nixGL's GL env now reaches host Arch binaries through Orca's terminals.** (orca.nix:221-224, together with the unsandboxing at :22-29)
The nixGL wrapper exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (nix mesa, libglvnd, mesa_glxindirect, vdpau), `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES`, `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH`, `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` and `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH`. The ELF is autoPatchelf'd and uses `runtimeDependencies` for libGL, so `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` isn't what lets Electron find its libraries. But every pty Orca spawns inherits all of it. Under bwrap the children ran the FHS env's nix userland, so this was harmless. Now they run Arch's `/usr/bin`.
- Failure scenario: nixpkgs glibc moves ahead of Arch's (today both are 2.44). Then any GL or VA program started from an Orca terminal (mpv, glxinfo, an Electron app, firefox via `xdg-open`) loads nix libglvnd or mesa and fails with `GLIBC_2.4x not found`. Or it runs nix mesa against host kernel and driver expectations.
- It works today by version coincidence.
- Fix options: document the trade-off in the comment, or check whether autoPatchelf + runtimeDependencies + `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH`/`GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` alone (no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) is enough for GPU rendering.
- `FONTCONFIG_FILE` leaks the same way. That isn't new (the old `--setenv` was inherited too), and host fontconfig is 2.18.3, the same as nix's. Low risk, but the same class of issue.

**I3. Removing AppRun is what closes Orca's fail-open `--no-sandbox` path. Nothing documents or tests that.** (orca.nix:69)
`resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/runtime/electron-sandbox-switch.js` has `shouldDisableExtractedAppImageSandbox`. If `dirname(executable)/AppRun` exists, Orca's CLI adds `--no-sandbox` whenever `unshare -Ur true` exits non-zero or throws (for example, `unshare` missing from PATH), and also when running as root.
- Today `rm -r .../{AppRun,...}` removes AppRun, so the path is dead. That's good, but the comment at :69 doesn't say it is load-bearing for security.
- Failure scenario: someone "simplifies" the rm list and keeps AppRun. Then `orca serve` or the CLI starts Electron without a sandbox, silently.
- On the rest of the sandbox claim: with userns available (`unprivileged_userns_clone=1`, `max_user_namespaces` large), Chromium uses the namespace sandbox. Without userns it reaches the non-setuid chrome-sandbox and aborts (FATAL "SUID sandbox helper ... not configured correctly"). That fails closed, not open.
- All BrowserWindows in app.asar use `sandbox:!0`. The only other app-side `--no-sandbox` path is env-driven (`APPIMAGE`, `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX`). The wrapper sets neither, and it doesn't scrub them either (nit).
- Fix: add "AppRun must stay out: its presence makes Orca's CLI fall back to --no-sandbox" to the comment, and add a non-GUI test assertion `[ ! -e "$APP/AppRun" ]`.

**I4. The default test run never checks the Chromium sandbox.** (tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:155-201)
Only the opt-in case 6 (ORCA_TEST_GUI=1) checks renderer namespaces. A regression that adds `--no-sandbox` (to the wrapper flags, or via I3) passes the default suite. The I3 assertion is a cheap partial guard. The namespace check itself is a fair proxy for layer 1: with `--no-sandbox`, renderers share the browser's user namespace, so the check fails. It does not show seccomp-bpf (layer 2). Also check `grep -q '^Seccomp:[[:space:]]*2' /proc/$p/status` for each renderer.

**I5. Build-output checks live in a post-hoc script, against the repo's stated convention.** (README.md:102-105, tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:70-75, :117-150)
The README says "what a build produced belongs to that derivation's own `installCheckPhase`, where it gates the build". Case 5 (pinned trees byte-identical, node sha256 vs `.runtime-node`) and case 1 (closure) are pure build-output properties. As written, a build that breaks the pin still installs and goes live, and only a manual test run notices. Do the `diff -r $src/resources/{node-runtime,orcad-template}` and the sha256 comparison at the end of `postFixup` (or in `installCheckPhase`), so a bad build fails.

## Nits

**N1. orca.nix:60-63: `patchShebangs` and `patchELF` still run over the pinned trees.**
The comment says rewriting fixups are "run by hand, or not at all", but `dontPatchShebangs` is unset. `orcad-template/out/cli/index.js` (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) and `orcad-template/computer-use-linux/runtime.py` (`python3`) survive only because neither interpreter is on the builder's PATH. I confirmed with `diff -r` against the src (k0m448...-extracted) that both trees are byte-identical today.
- Failure scenario: someone adds `nodejs` or `python3` to nativeBuildInputs (for example, to asar-inspect). The shebangs get rewritten to store paths, and template builds shipped to remote hosts break.
- Test case 5 would catch it, but only after the fact.
- Fix: set `dontPatchShebangs = true`, run `patchShebangs` on `targets` by hand, and say so in the comment.

**N2. orca.nix:96-97 "Orca's CLI runs this binary that way" is at best unverified.**
The bundled CLI (`resources/bin/orca-ide`) execs `$APP_DIR/orca-ide`, which is the raw `lib/orca/orca-ide` ELF and not the wrapper. When the CLI starts the GUI, it uses `process.execPath` (`orca-app-executable.js`), which is also the raw ELF. So a CLI-launched GUI (`orca serve` / open from a plain shell via the `~/.local/bin/orca-ide` CliInstaller symlink) gets no `--ozone-platform=wayland`, no `FONTCONFIG_FILE` and no nixGL env. It inherits them only when the CLI itself runs from an Orca terminal. That is pre-existing behaviour, but the comment implies the wrapper is on that path. If some other tool runs `bin/orca-ide` with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, name it. The same wording appears in the test at :81.

**N3. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:66: `mktemp` isn't checked.**
If `~/.cache` is missing, `T` is empty, and case 6 runs with `HOME=/home` and `--user-data-dir=/profile`. Add `|| exit 1`. Also say why it's under `~/.cache` and not `/tmp` (presumably so it's the same dir inside the old sandbox and in the host unit).

**N4. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:66, :162-164: the EXIT trap doesn't stop the transient unit.**
Ctrl-C during case 6's 40s wait leaves a visible second Orca instance running, with HOME in a directory the trap just `rm -rf`'d. Add `systemctl --user stop "$unit"` to the trap once `unit` is set.

**N5. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:157: the Wayland check reads the wrong env when not sandboxed.**
On the direct path, `host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY` reads the script's env. The systemd-run unit gets the user manager's env. If the manager env lacks `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the check says "go" and the launch fails as a "window" FAIL. Check with `systemctl --user show-environment` instead.

**N6. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:163: `--property=KillSignal=SIGTERM` is systemd's default.** It's redundant. Harmless, but it reads as if it changes something.

**N7. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:42-49: the `host()`/systemd-run branch only matters from a terminal of the old bwrap build.** Once this build is live, that branch is dead. That's fine as a transition aid, but a "drop once no bwrap build is running" note would stop it from fossilizing.

**N8. Existing env-driven sandbox switches aren't scrubbed.** `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX`, `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX` and `APPIMAGE`, if present in the user's env, would disable the sandbox or change behaviour. That isn't new, and only a user-controlled env reaches it. Optionally add `--unset` for them in makeWrapper.

**N9. Pre-existing:** `resources/package-type` is `AppImage`, so Orca's updater runs in "non-root" self-update mode against a read-only store path. It isn't new, just worth knowing.

## Checked and fine
- The wrapper (inner bin/orca-ide) is a plain `exec`. The node-mode guard treats empty `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` as unset, which matches Electron's own non-empty check.
- The comments at orca.nix:128 ("shared by orca and macKeybindings", used at :45 and :177) and :221-223 (nixGL) are accurate after the change.
- The test's writes: cases 2-4 run node mode with the real HOME. They write nothing except the fontconfig cache under `~/.cache/fontconfig` (benign). Case 6 isolates `~/.orca` and `~/.claude` via HOME and `--user-data-dir`. The user manager env has no `XDG_*_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` that would bypass the HOME override. `rm -rf "$T"` is quoted and `T` is mktemp-scoped (but see N3).

## Would the tests fail on regression?
| Regression | Caught? |
|---|---|
| Back to wrapType2/bwrap | yes: case 1 (closure), case 3 (hostname/zone from a child) |
| Wrapper injects ozone flag in node mode | yes: case 2 |
| `FONTCONFIG_FILE` dropped | yes: case 3 DejaVu (host has no DejaVu) |
| `dontStrip`/autoPatchelf exclusion removed, shebangs rewritten | yes: case 5 diff + pin (but after the fact; see I5, N1) |
| Missing runtime lib | partly: case 4 checks link-time deps only. Missing dlopened libs (libsecret, libnotify, libGL) are not caught |
| `--no-sandbox` / AppRun restored | only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 (case 6), and AppRun not at all; see I3, I4 |
| SIGTERM / exit-code passthrough | only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 |
EOF
echo done

No other stale bwrap, extraInstallCommands or sandbox-fonts references are left in tracked files (the .drovr/ hits are review artifacts).

**I2. nixGL's GL env now reaches host Arch binaries through Orca's terminals.** (orca.nix:221-224, together with the unsandboxing at :22-29)
The nixGL wrapper exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (nix mesa, libglvnd, mesa_glxindirect, vdpau), `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES`, `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH`, `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` and `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH`. The ELF is autoPatchelf'd and uses `runtimeDependencies` for libGL, so `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` isn't what lets Electron find its libraries. But every pty Orca spawns inherits all of it. Under bwrap the children ran the FHS env's nix userland, so this was harmless. Now they run Arch's `/usr/bin`.
- Failure scenario: nixpkgs glibc moves ahead of Arch's (today both are 2.44). Then any GL or VA program started from an Orca terminal (mpv, glxinfo, an Electron app, firefox via `xdg-open`) loads nix libglvnd or mesa and fails with `GLIBC_2.4x not found`. Or it runs nix mesa against host kernel and driver expectations.
- It works today by version coincidence.
- Fix options: document the trade-off in the comment, or check whether autoPatchelf + runtimeDependencies + `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH`/`GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` alone (no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) is enough for GPU rendering.
- `FONTCONFIG_FILE` leaks the same way. That isn't new (the old `--setenv` was inherited too), and host fontconfig is 2.18.3, the same as nix's. Low risk, but the same class of issue.

**I3. Removing AppRun is what closes Orca's fail-open `--no-sandbox` path. Nothing documents or tests that.** (orca.nix:69)
`resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/runtime/electron-sandbox-switch.js` has `shouldDisableExtractedAppImageSandbox`. If `dirname(executable)/AppRun` exists, Orca's CLI adds `--no-sandbox` whenever `unshare -Ur true` exits non-zero or throws (for example, `unshare` missing from PATH), and also when running as root.
- Today `rm -r .../{AppRun,...}` removes AppRun, so the path is dead. That's good, but the comment at :69 doesn't say it is load-bearing for security.
- Failure scenario: someone "simplifies" the rm list and keeps AppRun. Then `orca serve` or the CLI starts Electron without a sandbox, silently.
- On the rest of the sandbox claim: with userns available (`unprivileged_userns_clone=1`, `max_user_namespaces` large), Chromium uses the namespace sandbox. Without userns it reaches the non-setuid chrome-sandbox and aborts (FATAL "SUID sandbox helper ... not configured correctly"). That fails closed, not open.
- All BrowserWindows in app.asar use `sandbox:!0`. The only other app-side `--no-sandbox` path is env-driven (`APPIMAGE`, `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX`). The wrapper sets neither, and it doesn't scrub them either (nit).
- Fix: add "AppRun must stay out: its presence makes Orca's CLI fall back to --no-sandbox" to the comment, and add a non-GUI test assertion `[ ! -e "$APP/AppRun" ]`.

**I4. The default test run never checks the Chromium sandbox.** (tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:155-201)
Only the opt-in case 6 (ORCA_TEST_GUI=1) checks renderer namespaces. A regression that adds `--no-sandbox` (to the wrapper flags, or via I3) passes the default suite. The I3 assertion is a cheap partial guard. The namespace check itself is a fair proxy for layer 1: with `--no-sandbox`, renderers share the browser's user namespace, so the check fails. It does not show seccomp-bpf (layer 2). Also check `grep -q '^Seccomp:[[:space:]]*2' /proc/$p/status` for each renderer.

**I5. Build-output checks live in a post-hoc script, against the repo's stated convention.** (README.md:102-105, tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:70-75, :117-150)
The README says "what a build produced belongs to that derivation's own `installCheckPhase`, where it gates the build". Case 5 (pinned trees byte-identical, node sha256 vs `.runtime-node`) and case 1 (closure) are pure build-output properties. As written, a build that breaks the pin still installs and goes live, and only a manual test run notices. Do the `diff -r $src/resources/{node-runtime,orcad-template}` and the sha256 comparison at the end of `postFixup` (or in `installCheckPhase`), so a bad build fails.

## Nits

**N1. orca.nix:60-63: `patchShebangs` and `patchELF` still run over the pinned trees.**
The comment says rewriting fixups are "run by hand, or not at all", but `dontPatchShebangs` is unset. `orcad-template/out/cli/index.js` (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) and `orcad-template/computer-use-linux/runtime.py` (`python3`) survive only because neither interpreter is on the builder's PATH. I confirmed with `diff -r` against the src (k0m448...-extracted) that both trees are byte-identical today.
- Failure scenario: someone adds `nodejs` or `python3` to nativeBuildInputs (for example, to asar-inspect). The shebangs get rewritten to store paths, and template builds shipped to remote hosts break.
- Test case 5 would catch it, but only after the fact.
- Fix: set `dontPatchShebangs = true`, run `patchShebangs` on `targets` by hand, and say so in the comment.

**N2. orca.nix:96-97 "Orca's CLI runs this binary that way" is at best unverified.**
The bundled CLI (`resources/bin/orca-ide`) execs `$APP_DIR/orca-ide`, which is the raw `lib/orca/orca-ide` ELF and not the wrapper. When the CLI starts the GUI, it uses `process.execPath` (`orca-app-executable.js`), which is also the raw ELF. So a CLI-launched GUI (`orca serve` / open from a plain shell via the `~/.local/bin/orca-ide` CliInstaller symlink) gets no `--ozone-platform=wayland`, no `FONTCONFIG_FILE` and no nixGL env. It inherits them only when the CLI itself runs from an Orca terminal. That is pre-existing behaviour, but the comment implies the wrapper is on that path. If some other tool runs `bin/orca-ide` with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, name it. The same wording appears in the test at :81.

**N3. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:66: `mktemp` isn't checked.**
If `~/.cache` is missing, `T` is empty, and case 6 runs with `HOME=/home` and `--user-data-dir=/profile`. Add `|| exit 1`. Also say why it's under `~/.cache` and not `/tmp` (presumably so it's the same dir inside the old sandbox and in the host unit).

**N4. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:66, :162-164: the EXIT trap doesn't stop the transient unit.**
Ctrl-C during case 6's 40s wait leaves a visible second Orca instance running, with HOME in a directory the trap just `rm -rf`'d. Add `systemctl --user stop "$unit"` to the trap once `unit` is set.

**N5. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:157: the Wayland check reads the wrong env when not sandboxed.**
On the direct path, `host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY` reads the script's env. The systemd-run unit gets the user manager's env. If the manager env lacks `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the check says "go" and the launch fails as a "window" FAIL. Check with `systemctl --user show-environment` instead.

**N6. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:163: `--property=KillSignal=SIGTERM` is systemd's default.** It's redundant. Harmless, but it reads as if it changes something.

**N7. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:42-49: the `host()`/systemd-run branch only matters from a terminal of the old bwrap build.** Once this build is live, that branch is dead. That's fine as a transition aid, but a "drop once no bwrap build is running" note would stop it from fossilizing.

**N8. Existing env-driven sandbox switches aren't scrubbed.** `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX`, `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX` and `APPIMAGE`, if present in the user's env, would disable the sandbox or change behaviour. That isn't new, and only a user-controlled env reaches it. Optionally add `--unset` for them in makeWrapper.

**N9. Pre-existing:** `resources/package-type` is `AppImage`, so Orca's updater runs in "non-root" self-update mode against a read-only store path. It isn't new, just worth knowing.

## Checked and fine
- The wrapper (inner bin/orca-ide) is a plain `exec`. The node-mode guard treats empty `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` as unset, which matches Electron's own non-empty check.
- The comments at orca.nix:128 ("shared by orca and macKeybindings", used at :45 and :177) and :221-223 (nixGL) are accurate after the change.
- The test's writes: cases 2-4 run node mode with the real HOME. They write nothing except the fontconfig cache under `~/.cache/fontconfig` (benign). Case 6 isolates `~/.orca` and `~/.claude` via HOME and `--user-data-dir`. The user manager env has no `XDG_*_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` that would bypass the HOME override. `rm -rf "$T"` is quoted and `T` is mktemp-scoped (but see N3).

## Would the tests fail on regression?
| Regression | Caught? |
|---|---|
| Back to wrapType2/bwrap | yes: case 1 (closure), case 3 (hostname/zone from a child) |
| Wrapper injects ozone flag in node mode | yes: case 2 |
| `FONTCONFIG_FILE` dropped | yes: case 3 DejaVu (host has no DejaVu) |
| `dontStrip`/autoPatchelf exclusion removed, shebangs rewritten | yes: case 5 diff + pin (but after the fact; see I5, N1) |
| Missing runtime lib | partly: case 4 checks link-time deps only. Missing dlopened libs (libsecret, libnotify, libGL) are not caught |
| `--no-sandbox` / AppRun restored | only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 (case 6), and AppRun not at all; see I3, I4 |
| SIGTERM / exit-code passthrough | only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 |
EOF
echo done

content.text:
I found no Critical issues, five Important ones and nine nits. The Chromium sandbox claim holds: when the sandbox can't start, the app refuses to start rather than running without one. But the safeguard that keeps it that way is neither documented nor tested.

I checked the working tree (clean), the full diff, and the built output: `/nix/store/REDACTED.4.238` is the nixGL wrapper, and the real build is `/nix/store/hpcdlg163wysqyp2qy55xpqql3776sdk-orca-1.4.238`. I also searched `app.asar` and the bundled CLI sources. I did not launch the GUI.

## Critical
None.

## Important

**I1. `README.md:112` still lists the deleted `tests/sandbox-fonts.sh`.**
- It's described as "orca's real bwrap launcher resolves...". Anyone running the listed tests gets "No such file".
- No other stale bwrap, extraInstallCommands or sandbox-fonts references remain in tracked files, apart from the `.drovr/` review artifacts.

**I2. The nixGL GL environment now reaches host Arch programs through Orca's terminals** (`orca.nix:221-224`, combined with the change at `:22-29`).
- The nixGL wrapper exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (nix mesa, libglvnd, mesa_glxindirect, vdpau), `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES`, `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH`, `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` and `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH`.
- Every terminal Orca opens inherits these. Under bwrap, terminals ran the sandbox's nix programs, so this was harmless. Now they run Arch's `/usr/bin`.
- **Failure scenario:** once nixpkgs' glibc is newer than Arch's (both are 2.44 today), GL or video programs started from an Orca terminal fail with `GLIBC_2.4x not found`. Examples: mpv, glxinfo, Electron apps, firefox via `xdg-open`. Or they quietly run nix's mesa.
- It works today only because the versions happen to match. Either document the trade-off or test whether GPU rendering works without `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, since the binary is already patched.
- `FONTCONFIG_FILE` leaks the same way, but that isn't new: the old `--setenv` was inherited too. Host fontconfig is 2.18.3, the same as nix's.

**I3. Deleting `AppRun` is what keeps Orca from running without a sandbox. Neither the comment nor the test says so** (`orca.nix:69`).
- In `resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/runtime/electron-sandbox-switch.js`, if `AppRun` sits next to the executable, Orca's CLI adds `--no-sandbox` whenever `unshare -Ur true` fails or throws (including when `unshare` isn't on PATH), and whenever it runs as root.
- The `rm -r .../{AppRun,...}` line removes it today. If someone later trims that list and keeps `AppRun`, `orca serve` or a CLI-started GUI runs unsandboxed with no warning.
- The rest of the claim holds:
  - With user namespaces available (`unprivileged_userns_clone=1`, `max_user_namespaces=2147483647`), Chromium uses its namespace sandbox.
  - Without them, it hits the non-setuid `chrome-sandbox` and aborts. That fails closed.
  - Every BrowserWindow in `app.asar` sets `sandbox:!0`.
- **Fix:** say in the comment that `AppRun` must stay out, and add a test check `[ ! -e "$APP/AppRun" ]`.

**I4. A default test run never checks the Chromium sandbox** (`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:155-201`).
- Only the opt-in case 6 (`ORCA_TEST_GUI=1`) checks it, so a regression that adds `--no-sandbox` passes the default run.
- The user-namespace check is a fair test of Chromium's first sandbox layer, since `--no-sandbox` renderers share the main process's namespace. It doesn't cover the seccomp layer: also check each renderer's `/proc/$p/status` for `Seccomp: 2`.

**I5. The build-output checks run after the fact, against the README's own rule** (`README.md:102-105`, test `:70-75` and `:117-150`).
- The README says build checks belong in the derivation's `installCheckPhase`, where they stop a bad build.
- Two checks only inspect the build:
  - Case 5: the pinned trees diff, and node's sha256 against `.runtime-node`.
  - Case 1: bubblewrap in the closure.
- As written, a build that breaks the pin still installs and goes live. Move the `diff -r` and sha256 check into `postFixup` or `installCheckPhase`.

## Nits
- **N1.** `orca.nix:60-63`: the fixup step that rewrites `#!` lines still runs over the pinned trees (`dontPatchShebangs` is unset). Two files there survive only because `node` and `python3` aren't on the build PATH: `orcad-template/out/cli/index.js` (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) and `computer-use-linux/runtime.py`. I confirmed with `diff -r` against the extracted AppImage that both trees are byte-identical today. Adding nodejs or python3 to the build inputs would silently break the remote template builds; only test case 5 would notice, after install.
- **N2.** `orca.nix:96-97` (and test `:81`) say "Orca's CLI runs this binary that way", which looks inaccurate. The bundled CLI `resources/bin/orca-ide` runs the raw `lib/orca/orca-ide`, and a CLI-started GUI uses `process.execPath`, also raw. So those launches get no ozone flag, no `FONTCONFIG_FILE` and no nixGL environment, unless they inherit them from an Orca terminal. That predates this change.
- **N3.** Test `:66`: the `mktemp` result isn't checked. If `~/.cache` is missing, `T` is empty and case 6 runs with `HOME=/home` and `--user-data-dir=/profile`. A comment on why it uses `~/.cache` rather than `/tmp` would also help.
- **N4.** Test `:66` and `:162-164`: the exit trap doesn't stop the transient systemd unit. Ctrl-C during case 6 leaves a visible second Orca running with its HOME already deleted.
- **N5.** Test `:157`: when not sandboxed, `host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY` reads the script's environment, but the systemd-run unit gets the user manager's. Check `systemctl --user show-environment` instead.
- **N6.** Test `:163`: `KillSignal=SIGTERM` is already systemd's default, so it's redundant.
- **N7.** Test `:42-49`: the `systemd-run` path only matters when run from an old bwrap build's terminal. A note to drop it later would keep it from lingering.
- **N8.** The wrapper doesn't clear `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX`, `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX` or `APPIMAGE` from the user's environment. Not new, and only the user can set them.
- **N9.** Not new: `resources/package-type` is `AppImage`, so Orca's updater runs in self-update mode against a read-only store path.

## Checked and fine
- The wrapper is a plain `exec`. Its node-mode guard treats an empty `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` as unset, matching Electron.
- The comments at `orca.nix:128` and `:221-223` are accurate after the change.
- Cases 2-4 use the real HOME but write only the fontconfig cache. Case 6 keeps away from the real `~/.orca` and `~/.claude` through its HOME override and `--user-data-dir`. The user manager sets no `XDG_*_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` that would get around that. `rm -rf "$T"` is quoted and safe, apart from N3.

## Would the tests fail on regression?

| Regression | Caught? |
|---|---|
| Back to the bwrap wrapper | Yes: cases 1 and 3 |
| Ozone flag added in node mode | Yes: case 2 |
| `FONTCONFIG_FILE` dropped | Yes: case 3's DejaVu check |
| Pinned trees stripped, patched or with `#!` lines rewritten | Yes: case 5, but only after install (I5, N1) |
| Missing runtime libraries | Partly: case 4 checks linked libraries only. Libraries loaded at runtime (libsecret, libnotify, libGL) aren't checked. |
| `--no-sandbox` or `AppRun` restored | Only with `ORCA_TEST_GUI=1`; `AppRun` not at all (I3, I4) |
| SIGTERM and exit-code passthrough | Only with `ORCA_TEST_GUI=1` |

The findings are also saved at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-sauyon-orca-workspaces-dotfiles-orca-gui-unsandbox/0f356773-2907-467c-ac73-3e2219018d85/scratchpad/review-r1-security.md`.
